messages:
elaine: FYI escalation from legal — customer claims a user who was deprovisioned via SCIM still had access for ~3 hours and is requesting retention evidence and key unwrap logs. Need triage.

josh: ack. customer, org-id 12345? do we have the SCIM webhook delivery logs and the user change in our provisioning queue?

elaine: org-id 12345. They attached a screenshot showing the app activity at 2024-06-14T22:41Z. They say SCIM deprov job ran at 19:05Z.

maria: I can check provisioning queue and auth logs. quick question — do they want full KMS unwrap events (HSM logs) or just audit export of user->token mappings? Legal asked for both.

elaine: legal requested: (1) SCIM deprovisioning event payload + delivery status, (2) auth tokens issued/expired for that user, (3) KMS/HSM unwrap events showing whether any keys were used to access customer blobs after deprov, and (4) retention proof that deleted content was removed per policy.

josh: Note: HSM/UWrap logs are sensitive. We need samir (security) approval and a ticket to request limited export. @samir can you sign off and indicate required format?

samir: I approve access for a scoped export limited to org 12345 and window 2024-06-14T18:00Z->2024-06-14T23:59Z. Provide justification in ticket, include legal contact. Preferred format: CSV with columns: time, event_type, key_id (truncated), actor, request_id. I will run scrubber for key material.

maria: repro steps I'm running now:
1) query provisioning queue: `SELECT * FROM scim_events WHERE org_id=12345 AND user_email='banned@example.com' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;`
2) auth log search: `grep 'banned@example.com' /var/log/auth-proxy/2024-06-14.log | sed -n '1,200p'`
3) ksm unwrap audit: `redwood-audit query --org 12345 --event unwrap --start '2024-06-14T18:00' --end '2024-06-14T23:59'`

elaine: small ask from legal: include any delivery/retry headers for SCIM (HTTP 2xx vs 5xx) and webhook response bodies if we have them. Also they want token introspection results for any tokens issued after deprov.

audit-bot: Automated note: audit export request created: EX-3819 by elaine. Status: pending security approval.

josh: I see one suspicious entry — provisioning queue shows a failed webhook at 19:06:12 (502). But a retry at 19:07:30 shows 200. Need to confirm whether the downstream app processed the 200 or if that was acceptance-only. Can we get SCIM response bodies?

maria: Found auth logs: there are 3 token uses for banned@example.com at 20:13:07, 20:14:22, and 21:01:03. Token IDs: tok_***a9c. Request IDs attached in logs. I'll add them to EX-3819.

elaine: legal flagged billing impact too — they want a breakdown of any feature usage billed after deprov window. Can billing export be appended?

samir: yes, add billing export for that org for 2024-06-14. Ensure PII is redacted. I'll approve once ticket includes legal contact and export scope.

josh: one more edge: KMS unwrap tool returns no unwrap events for key_id starting with k-9e after 20:00Z. Maria, can you paste the raw unwrap query output to the ticket (masked) and indicate if any unwraps exist after the last token use?

maria: pasted into EX-3819: `time,event,key_id,actor,request_id
2024-06-14T20:13:07,unwrap,k-9e***,service-account-uploads,req-3344
2024-06-14T21:01:03,unwrap,k-9e***,service-account-uploads,req-4411`

elaine: Legal will want a short timeline in plain language. I'll draft: "SCIM deprov webhook sent 19:05Z -> retry succeeded 19:07Z -> token activity observed 20:13Z and 21:01Z -> KMS unwraps correlate to those requests, indicating background job used cached token material." Can someone confirm cached session TTL & whether indexer jobs use service-account tokens post-deprov?

josh: Cached session TTL for tokens is 1h by default; some internal indexer jobs use service-account tokens that can access org blobs — if the background job used a service-account with prior access, that could explain post-deprov access. Need to check if those unwraps were service-account vs user token.

maria: logs show actor=service-account-uploads for both unwraps. So likely background job. We should include that in the timeline and suggest mitigations: shorten cache TTL, rotate service-account keys, and block in-flight jobs on deprov via an admission webhook.

elaine: thanks all. I'll update legal and attach EX-3819 exports when samir signs off. :thumbsup:

samir: Signed off. Proceed with scoped export. Make sure to mark ticket SENSITIVE and notify compliance.
